title: Fault Night
hook: A late shift, more faults than teams. What is behind each, only a look will tell.
text: 22:00 to 22:40 in the maintenance control centre of the district around Bf Neustadt, alone, and on the lab's table: faults light up where their assets are, and what is behind each is known only when a team has looked. Two emergency teams are on shift, one for signalling and one for the track, and a technician of each trade is on call. Rank the faults, send the vans, ask the signaller for a closure before anybody works in the track, and decide what a team does with what it finds: a repair for good, a quick one that may not hold, or guarding a danger until the right team comes.

story.say: Late shift. Two vans at the base: mine for signalling, L. Kranich's for the track. When a fault lights up on the table, tap it, then the van to send. We only know what it is once we have looked.
Before anybody works in the track, the signaller has to close it. Ask for the closure first. I am not sending my people out otherwise.
A red ring is a danger with nobody there. Any of us can stand guard until the right team comes. But whoever guards repairs nothing.
A quick repair gets the trains running now. It may not hold. A repair for good takes longer and holds. Your call, every time.
Two technicians are on call at home. Tap the base to wake one: four hours of overtime, and ten minutes until they are ready. Worth it only if they still repair something tonight.

debrief: Which fault did you send a team to first, and why? What did the faults that waited cost?
A team stood at the signal and the work was in track G2. Who may close a track, and what could have happened without the closure?
Where did you send a team before you knew the cause? What did you go by, and was it the right trade?
A provisional repair or one for good: when was which the better choice, and what did it cost when it did not hold?
Was a technician on call worth the four hours of overtime?
